subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes the record of the quadrangle issue now exists and matters, regardless of whether Bahamut reads it.
source_quote: the record now exists, and the record says: the quadrangle issue landed.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is operating on an instinct that the one with Lesser Restoration isn't ready to spend it, and arguing won't make healing come sooner.
source_quote: Daral was operating on an instinct he couldn't quite articulate: that the one with the Lesser Restoration wasn't ready to spend it, and that arguing wouldn't make the healing come any sooner.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is concerned that Daral, once restored, would disappear and become difficult to locate because he might have already shared his most valuable information.
source_quote: The concern was that Daral, once restored, would discover pressing business elsewhere and become difficult to locate. The ones who ran the moment they felt better were usually the ones who'd shared their most valuable information right before the healing, because they knew they wouldn't be around to see how you used it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalls that someone like Daral had already been sent away from their party.
source_quote: Didn't we have somebody like that with our party anyhow? Did we already send him away?

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool remembers when there was cheese and grieves its absence.
source_quote: I remember when there was cheese. Perhaps if we had some cheese.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool believes he could have eaten through Alkrist's safe, though it would have taken a while.
source_quote: I guess I could have eaten through the safe. It would have taken a while.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir refuses to punch the safe because they were trying to be sneaky, not destructive.
source_quote: If the goal was to be destructive, I could've just punched the safe. But we were trying to be sneaky.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool believes walls do not stop him and that he can eat through them.
source_quote: Walls don't stop us. I can eat through walls.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thinks the poison book method was too elaborate, which is exactly why it worked.
source_quote: Poisoned book, frames a colleague, and disappears the evidence. Too elaborate. Which is exactly why it worked.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin realizes that magic like Speak with Dead cannot be relied upon because the dead are still themselves and may misremember or misattribute events.
source_quote: Well, I'm interested — even if we were able to actually cast Speak with Dead, how do you know they're a reliable narrator? What are their motivations after they're dead? We don't know. Because they're dead.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin understands that the myth of the person — the assumption that death brings transparency — is false.
source_quote: The myth of the person. The assumption that death is a transparency, that the dead have shed their performances and will now simply tell you what's true. They don't. They're still themselves.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin recalls that in the Underdark, the only thing that didn't lie was terrain — the fixed physical world.
source_quote: In the Underdark, the one thing that didn't lie was terrain. You couldn't trust what you were told. You couldn't trust what you saw. But the ground under your feet was fixed.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin remembers that giants taught him the principle that a rock's meaning depends on its placement — not its nature.
source_quote: Giants taught me that without ever writing it down. A rock in the wrong place is just a rock. A rock in the right place is a wall.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realizes that the Sylvira lookalike's appearances create a two-hour gap that cannot be explained by a single polymorph spell.
source_quote: The Sylvira lookalike had been seen in the kitchens around one in the morning. She'd been seen coming down the stairs between two and three. That's a minimum two-hour gap. A polymorph spell lasts an hour.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir suspects something more than a simple polymorph — or repeated use of it — is involved in the Sylvira lookalike sightings.
source_quote: Something more is going on here.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir has been quiet because he is working through a problem until it is finished.
source_quote: Zalthir had been quiet for a while, which with Zalthir means he's working something through until it's finished.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed the dragonborn quality in Alkrist the way he notices the size of a room before noticing the people in it.
source_quote: I noticed this the way I notice the size of a room before I notice the people in it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed he could use the dragonborn conversational bond with Alkrist.
source_quote: I knew I could.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir silently approved of Grygum's decision to investigate the third-story apartment.
source_quote: I approved of it silently.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thought the apartment in Janussi's chambers held evidence about Kalan that didn't need an interview to yield.
source_quote: There was still evidence about Kalan we hadn't turned over. The kind of thing that didn't need an interview to yield.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recalled Brother Heslin or Brother Varath teaching the art of the urgent errand.
source_quote: Brother Heslin, or possibly Brother Varath, I'm genuinely uncertain which, had devoted an entire season to teaching our cohort the art of the urgent errand, the clean dispatch.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed that Fembris operated with monastic commitment to immediate tasks.
source_quote: There is something almost monastic about how Fembris operates: the total commitment to the immediate task, no friction between decision and movement.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noted that Daz was the natural choice to interview Sylvira because he knew how to make someone talk and was drow.
source_quote: I noted this and did not say it aloud.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir had not flagged the detail about what Alkrist burned at the feast.
source_quote: I hadn't flagged that one.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was working through the zone-of-truth timing and dragonborn opening when Kalan would arrive.
source_quote: I had been working through the zone-of-truth timing, the dragonborn opening, when Kalan would arrive.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum remembered that Alkrist had burned something at the feast and wanted Zalthir to ask about it.
source_quote: When you talk to Alkrist, there's something in the list about what Alkrist burned at the feast — you should ask about that.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum felt it was rude to notice the private arrangements in Janussi's third-story apartment.
source_quote: I poked around, maybe a little cautiously, because you never know if you're going to find something you'd rather not, but I looked... More like walking in on someone's private arrangements and feeling vaguely rude about noticing them.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recognized the academic insult genre in Janussi's writing.
source_quote: I've read enough Bahamut commentary, the kind written by scholars who've spent forty years sharpening the same argument against a rival they've never met, to recognize the genre.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realized Janussi had characterized Kalan's entire framework as solipsism.
source_quote: Janussi had reviewed Kalan Strongbranch's proposal for new criminal investigation methodologies, found it to be solipsism, and had blocked it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum understood that Janussi's rejection of Kalan’s work was a quiet, contemptuous cruelty.
source_quote: Not the cruelty that shouts. The cruelty that doesn't bother being angry at you.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum concluded that Kalan built his methodology in the wreckage of Janussi's rejection.
source_quote: It means he built his whole methodology in the wreckage of the man who told him he was wrong.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that Janussi had dismissed Kalan’s work as an indulgence and a conceit.
source_quote: As though the investigation of crime were an indulgence, a hobby, a *conceit* Kalan was pursuing for his own entertainment at the institution's expense.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed Sylvira was using a mage hand despite being bedridden and shuddering with fever.
source_quote: A mage hand, which was interesting: she was bedridden and shuddering under a fever, and still running a familiar and a mage hand from across the room.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz filed Sylvira's use of mage hand under 'not incapacitated.'
source_quote: I filed that in the column marked *not incapacitated.*

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observed that Sylvira showed relief beneath her shock and upset.
source_quote: Underneath both was something she hadn't meant to let through: relief.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized Sylvira's compliment about him leading the investigation was a strategic move.
source_quote: I filed the compliment and moved on.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understood that Sylvira's suspicion of Menzoberranzan tactics was reasonable given her background.
source_quote: The suspicion was entirely reasonable: the city I came from is not known for delivering bad news to people out of charitable concern.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognized that Sylvira's mention of Kazryn Nyantani carried deep emotional weight.
source_quote: The name arrived with a weight that told me it had been sitting just below the surface.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed Sylvira broke down genuinely when speaking of Kazryn, not as performance.
source_quote: She broke down. Not performance; it came from somewhere real and arrived without warning.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understood that Sylvira believed she was being framed because of her infernal heritage and relationship with Janussi.
source_quote: In the Overbright, she said, people look at a tiefling and assume she's an abyssal spawn. She happened, technically, to be an abyssal spawn, so they weren't even wrong. Her area of research was the infernal domains, which compounded the prejudice. The relationship with Janussi had probably offended someone else on top of that.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized Sylvira's admission that she hadn't seen anyone in the morning was emotionally loaded.
source_quote: She started to say she couldn't say that she'd seen anyone, and then something caught in her throat.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognized that Sylvira's last words to Janussi were emotionally significant.
source_quote: Those were my last words with him.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz knew Sylvira was not responding to logic but to steadiness in her distress.
source_quote: She was distraught in the genuine, inconvenient way: the kind that doesn't respond to logic, only to steadiness.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed Sylvira's willingness to speak was genuine and not performative.
source_quote: I will not call her a mark. I will call her a witness.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira knew her field and dismissed Kalan Strongbranch's research as third-rate at best.
source_quote: Janussi was right to want him gone. He was a clown, a boar, and his research was third-rate at best.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira insisted she had never called Kalan Strongbranch a genus traitor.
source_quote: But she had never, she insisted, called him a genus traitor.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira anticipated being asked whether she called Kalan a genus traitor, which suggested she had prepared for the question.
source_quote: The word "never" had a specificity that suggested she'd anticipated being asked.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira had never drunk honey and felt genuine offense at the suggestion.
source_quote: Honey? I would never drink honey. What kind of nonsense is this?

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira believed that anyone claiming to have seen her after 12:30 was lying, and named Teles Ahvoste as a hostile party.
source_quote: it would be members of the avowed who had long nurtured hostility toward her. Great Readers included. She named Teles Ahvoste directly.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira believed jealousy was a powerful motivator for revenge and murder.
source_quote: Jealousy is a powerful motivator, she said. For revenge. Murder.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira considered Kalan Strongbranch's proposal insane and believed Bookwyrm had pushed hardest against it.
source_quote: his proposal, which she called insane, all sorts of investigative controls and restrictions. When Janussi had raised it at some point, it was Bookwyrm who'd felt it was absurd. Bookwyrm who had pushed hardest against it.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira was grieving the last argument she had had with her son.
source_quote: And a sick tiefling in a too-hot room, shivering despite the fire, grieving the last argument she'd had with someone she'd loved.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira had been trying to coax her son back into the Mordenkainen's Mansion she built for his protection.
source_quote: She'd been trying to coax him back into it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed a straight edge on the crumpled wrapping paper that shouldn't have been there.
source_quote: There was something else. A straight edge where there shouldn't be one.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled that Mending is a spell that can restore things to their original state.
source_quote: Oh, Mending is smart, I said, to nobody in particular. Let me see — do I have that one? I do.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realized the wrapping paper had been deliberately cut and then rewrapped, indicating preparation.
source_quote: Someone had taken something sharp to this paper, and then wrapped it back around the contents, and tied the bow, and handed it to Janussi, or left it on a table, or had it carried by someone who had no idea what they were carrying.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum understood that the crime was not one of opportunity but of preparation.
source_quote: That is not a crime of opportunity. That is a crime of preparation.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the perpetrator was calm, prepared, and patient, and had planned for what happened after Janussi's death.
source_quote: whoever did this was calm, prepared, and patient. They had planned for what happened after the gift was opened, which means they had planned for what happened after Janussi was dead.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir instinctively wanted to pin the timing down to the minute and never let a gap between two facts go unaccounted for.
source_quote: Zalthir's instinct would have been to pin the timing down to the minute. He never let a gap between two facts go unaccounted for.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed that what you find in someone's room tells you more than what they'd ever say with their face.
source_quote: I had been in Alkrist's chambers earlier, moving through the dark in a way I was reasonably confident he hadn't noticed. The book was on a shelf, bookmarked. I had read the section it was bookmarked to. There was a class at the monastery, Brother Essivhan, possibly, or the quiet one with the ink-stained hands, about what you find in someone's room telling you more than what they'd ever say with their face.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist believed he had a fantastic, superb relationship with Janussi.
source_quote: I was a big fan of Janussi — his leadership quality, and, let's be clear, I had a fantastic, superb relationship with the man.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist was self-absorbed enough to miss irony when it was directed at him.
source_quote: He took it as sincere. He was pleased. I filed it: self-absorption sufficient to blunt irony.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist was appalled when he learned Janussi's heart had been ripped out.
source_quote: Ripped out his heart? What? His heart was ripped out?

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist claimed he was under mind control and that everything he said was true against his will.
source_quote: I am under mind control, and everything I have said is so true.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist's hand drifted toward the shelf when asked which book he used for the murder method.
source_quote: His hand moved toward the shelf before his mouth had finished the sentence.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist realized he had accidentally revealed the bookmarked book and tried to stop the investigators from looking.
source_quote: Don't look, don't look, don't look!

subject: Alkrist's motive
fact: Alkrist resented Janussi for dismissing his germ warfare research and denying his leadership potential, but the full extent of his grievance remains unexplored.
source_quote: dismissed, told his germ warfare research was dangerous and should be stopped, told he showed no leadership potential.

subject: Bookwyrm's involvement
fact: Bookwyrm argued with Alkrist after learning of the poisoning and stormed off, but her subsequent actions and knowledge of the chalice remain unexplained.
source_quote: She went somewhere. He went home. Someone had known about the chalice: what it was for, what could be hidden inside it, why no one would think to look there without specific reason. That someone was not Alkrist.

subject: The chalice's origin
fact: The identity of the person who knew about the chalice and its hidden purpose remains unknown.
source_quote: Someone had known about the chalice: what it was for, what could be hidden inside it, why no one would think to look there without specific reason. That someone was not Alkrist.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir remembers that Brother Quellin or possibly Brother Harren said 'They all stabbed him.'
source_quote: Brother Quellin had said this. Or possibly Brother Harren, I was never certain of the attribution.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes the most dangerous person in a room is the one who has already decided they've won.
source_quote: The most dangerous person in a room isn't the one with the blade drawn. It's the one who has already decided they've won.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recognizes that A'lai needs discretion above all else.
source_quote: He needed, above all other things, discretion.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes blackmail is the most reliably underpriced resource in the world, especially in the hands of someone who desperately needs it.
source_quote: It is not expressed in gold... It is the most reliably underpriced resource in the world, especially in the hands of someone who desperately needs it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir has been maintaining a column since Kaelira told him someone powerful was paying to protect a man he couldn't understand.
source_quote: The column I had been maintaining since Kaelira told me bluntly that someone powerful was paying to protect a man she couldn't understand.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir has been unable to name the entity behind the patron entry in his column for months.
source_quote: The patron entry had been blank for months. Every time I thought I was close to something, it receded.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir considers A'lai the first real lead he's been offered since Kaelira laid out the problem.
source_quote: Now there was a compromised drow scholar who might represent the first real lead I'd been offered since Kaelira laid the problem out for me plainly.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir finds it uncomfortable to be the unknown variable in his own accounts.
source_quote: It is not comfortable to be the unknown variable in your own accounts.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes his training requires knowing where every debt is, who holds it, and what it costs.
source_quote: My training ran toward the opposite: know where every debt is, who holds it, what it costs.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir suspects A'lai constructed a narrative of administrative efficiency to justify Janussi’s death.
source_quote: The man who treats blackmail as a kind of career knows how to make his own history sound administrative.

subject: Zalthir's mission
fact: Zalthir has a mission in mind involving A'lai and the patron behind the unknown entity, but has not yet finalized the terms.
source_quote: I have a mission in mind.

subject: Zalthir's alternative proposal
fact: Zalthir is considering an alternative proposal where A'lai pays not in gold or books, but in information about the patron funding his survival.
source_quote: I had an alternative proposal forming. It was not finalized. But the terms were these: A'lai does not pay in gold, and does not pay in books. A'lai pays in what he knows. And what he knows about whoever is paying Menzoberranzan rates to keep a nobody drow evoker alive and functional: that is the only price I am interested in collecting.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes the team should give the evidence to Kalan so he can clean house.
source_quote: I think we go to the guy that was fired, give it to him, let him clean house.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin insists the team should get a book per suspect as compensation.
source_quote: I'm gonna insist that we get a book per suspect.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum suggests the team could blackmail one or more of the suspects.
source_quote: We could always decide to blackmail one or more of them.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observes that in murder mysteries, someone often treats blackmail as a kind of career.
source_quote: In these murder mysteries, you often find somebody who treats blackmail as a kind of career.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes Janussi had high intelligence but not high wisdom.
source_quote: Well, it's clear he may have high intelligence, but not high wisdom.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz needs information from A'lai, who is a drow with Underdark connections.
source_quote: A'lai, moreover, is a drow. He might have information that Daz needs.
